summary: The 13th Dalai Lama (1876–1933) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under Agvan Dorzhiev, Tertön Sogyal, Pa Ri Rabsal, and several other teachers, and taught numerous students, including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen.

Active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, the 14th Dalai Lama studied under teachers including Trijang Lobsang Yeshe Tenzin Gyatso and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists (1989) and Mind and Life Institute (1990).

Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) studied under Kalu Rinpoche, Beru Khyentse Rinpoche I, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He taught numerous students, including Reginald A. Ray, Tsultrim Allione, and Joseph Goldstein.
19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche (1917–2003) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen, Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso, and Khangsar Dorje Chang.

id: P:3rd Sras Rinpoche Thubten Kalsang Bstanpai Gyaltsen
summary: Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery, Gyume Tantric College, and under the 96th Ganden Tripa Thubten Kunga. He held posts at Drepung Loseling, Gyume Tantric College, and Rizong Monastery.

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied at Drepung Monastery (~1951–1959). He held positions at the Central School for Tibetans, Shimla (1960), the Central School for Tibetans (1965–1970), and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1971–2001).
A Drö Khenpo Yeshe Gyatso studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé (1895–1969) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Ayu Khandro, and taught Chatral Sangye Dorje and Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche.

A. A. Krishnaswami Ayyangar (1892–1953) studied at Pachaiyappa's College (~1908–1911). He held posts at Pachaiyappa's College (1911–1918) and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (1918–1947).
A. B. Gajendragadkar worked in Indology. He held posts as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College.
A. Charlene McDermott worked in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under W. Norman Brown and held an attested post at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee in 1969.

A scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology, Muller studied at Stony Brook, Virginia, and other institutions. He held posts at Toyo Gakuen University (1994–2008), the University of Tokyo (2005; 2008–2019), and Musashino University (2019), and founded H-Buddhism.
A. Fürst worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe.
A. G. Mohan (born 1945) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from ~1971 to 1989 and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

Armstrong (1909–1997) was a philosopher educated at Jesus College, Cambridge. He taught at Swansea, Malta, Beaumont College, Cardiff, Manhattanville, and Dalhousie, and was Gladstone Professor of Greek at Liverpool (1950–1972). He founded Dionysius in 1977.

A. I. Sabra (1924–2013) worked in philosophy and history and archaeology. He studied at Alexandria University, the University of London, and the London School of Economics under Karl Popper, later holding posts at the Warburg Institute and Harvard University.

A. K. Ramanujan (1929–1993) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Mysore and Indiana University Bloomington. He taught at Baroda and Deccan College before a long career as a professor at the University of Chicago (1962–1993).

A. Mahadeva Sastri (1861–1926) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (~1891–1916) and as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1916–1926).

A. N. Krishna Aiyangar worked in Indology and studied under K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar. He served as joint editor for Brahmavidya at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1950) and as librarian at the National Archives of India (attested 1954).

A. N. Narasimhia was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933). He held posts at the University of Mysore and Maharaja's College, Mysore.
